lesson.title: 5.1 A lot of apples, a few apples
lesson.unit_outcome: Say how much and how many, offer and order food and drinks politely, agree about likes, say what you want and need to do, talk about meals, prices and what is in your food, compare prices, use numbers to ninety-nine and ask for things at the table.
lesson.lesson_title: A lot of apples, a few apples
lesson.sub_lesson_title: A lot of apples, a few apples
lesson.goal: Say if there are a lot of or a few things (There are a lot of apples. / There are a few apples.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 5.1 Fruits: A1 names fruit and counts it with numbers (three apples); A1+ 5.1 says the amount without a number: a lot of for a big amount and a few for a small one, both before a plural (There are a lot of apples. / There are a few apples.), and a lot of before fruit as a whole (Diego eats a lot of fruit.). The photos show a big heap against three pieces of the same fruit, so each picture shows one amount. How many … are there? (A1 5.4) asks, and the reply gives the amount.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 5.1 fruit, apples, oranges, strawberries, bananas; A1 3.12 has; A1 5.4 How many … are there?; A1+ 1.2 eats.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Join a lot of into one phrase (a-LOT-of, of very short) and stress few in a few; do not require native-like speed.
